newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Coffee captures attention before expiry.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Coffee captures attention before expiry.

text.p: LIFFE coffee options mustered volume this week with November now heading towards expiry but cocoa offered little excitement in a rangebound futures market.
An impressive 1,140 lots traded in coffee options Wednesday mainly involving a fence on March $1,350 calls and $1,450 puts.

But less than two weeks before expiry, the spotlight was on November $1,600 calls which command a large open interest of 1,650 lots and could trigger delta hedging above current prices. "Once the $1,540 (level) breaks, $1,600 is not too far off," said one trader.

Coffee futures see-sawed this week after news of a big draw in U.S. certified stocks, raising the possibility of tight nearby supplies. But some analysts say upcoming Central American harvest may replenish low stocks and keep a lid on prices.
On options, November call volatilities have picked up slightly to 28-30 percent from 26 percent on Wednesday but brokers said prices were still on the cheap side for buyers.
"For bulls in November, swapping out their long futures with the call may be a cheap way to play the market," commodity house Sucden said in its daily commentary on Thursday.
But there were more sellers of at-the-money options than buyers while futures continued to swing in a tight corridor.
Rangebound futures also took the blame for dwindling demand in cocoa options after tension over the September futures delivery fizzled out.
"People are sitting on the fence," said one market maker.

Buyers were unenthusiastic while direction in futures remained blurred just days before the new marketing season starts in top producer Ivory Coast. Ivorian new crop arrivals may provide clues to the size of the main harvest after a series of forecasts since June which occupied a wide range.
March 1,100 stg calls saw mild interest earlier in the week when hopes for an upside break was still intact before the market began to drift.
But a good strategy recommended in a rangebound market is to sell the strangle on March. This involves selling the 950 put and the 1,100 call at the same time.

Traders also singled out March 950 put sell as an attractive deal but there were very few buyers. Implied volatilities stayed flat despite the continued pressure on March. Calls were around 20-21 percent, but 22 percent was fetched earlier this week.
"Not a bad sell if you think the market is rangebound," commented Sucden in a daily options report.
Puts were trading slightly lower at 18-19 percent volatility.
